newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH AKTIA SAYS LISTING PLAN STILL ON ICE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH AKTIA SAYS LISTING PLAN STILL ON ICE.

text.p: Finnish Aktia Bank's plan to seek a listing is currently on ice and since the bank does not need new capital it is a matter for the owners alone, CEO Johan Horelli said on Monday.
"We do not need capital ... a listing is an issue for the owners which is currently on ice," Horelli told Reuters.
Finnish savings bank foundations own 50.9 percent of Aktia and Swedish savings bank Swedbank owns 25 percent, with a view to help develop it, not take it over.

Aktia earlier reported more than doubled first-half earnings with operating profit at 30.3 million markka versus 14.3 million in the first half last year, and Horelli said the interim report confirmed a trend of falling credit losses.
Credit and guarantee losses fell to 23.6 million markka in January-June from 25.1 million in the year-ago period.
Horelli declined to give any more specific full-year 1997 forecasts than the bank's statement that earnings would continue to develop favourably during the rest of the year.
